dct_title_s: Nepal Flood 2026 Flood Affected Area, Bhote Koshi and Trishuli
dct_description_sm: OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps vector layers for the area flooded in the 2026 Bhote Koshi and Trishuli flood, Nepal, and the ground immediately around it. The area of interest is the observed flood extent of 27 August 2026 widened by 200 metres, 90.11 square kilometres in total. The flood extent was mapped from drone, Landsat, PlanetScope and Sentinel imagery and covers 31.70 square kilometres. It is published here as its own resource, so the water line can be separated from the margin around it. The 200 m margin includes buildings and roads next to the water, not only those in it. Being in this dataset does not mean a feature was flooded. Use the Flood Extent resource for the water only. The extent spans Bagmati and Gandaki Provinces, five districts, Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitawan, and sixteen municipalities, following the river from Rasuwagadhi to the Narayani confluence. Presence in this dataset does not by itself mean a feature was damaged or destroyed. Buildings mappers have recorded as destroyed are in a separate **Destroyed Buildings** layer. The `destroyed:` prefix replaces the plain `building` tag, so these are not in the Buildings layer. Read both together for the building stock before the flood. AI-scored building damage from post-event imagery is published separately as [Nepal Flood 2026: fAIr Damage Assessment](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl_buildings_damage). This is the close view, the flooded ground and a 200 m margin. **For the wider 1 km river corridor under assessment, 317 sq km from Rasuwagadhi to the Narayani confluence, use [Nepal Flood 2026 River Corridor](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl_corridor).** Every layer is published here as a resource, and most layers carry two versions, one from OpenStreetMap and one from Overture Maps. The two are not interchangeable: - **OpenStreetMap** layers are live. They are rebuilt every six hours, and each rebuild queries OpenStreetMap directly rather than reading a pre-cut country extract, so a layer reflects the map as it stood minutes before the file was written. Work done by volunteer mappers during the response shows up in the next rebuild. Use these when currency matters. - **Overture Maps** layers fuse building footprints and other features from Microsoft, Google and OpenStreetMap. That fusion gives broader coverage than OSM alone in places volunteers have not reached yet, but **Overture is not updated daily**. It follows Overture's own release cycle, so it will not reflect mapping done during this response and will fall progressively further behind the OpenStreetMap layers. In short, Overture is wider but older; OpenStreetMap is current. For damage assessment against the latest mapping, prefer the OpenStreetMap layers and treat Overture as a supplement where OSM coverage is thin. Mapping task boundaries from the Tasking Manager campaign are published here too and refreshed daily, showing where volunteers are being asked to map. The bridge damage assessment is reported from the ground by volunteers. It lists road bridges with their condition after the flood, deck length where measured, and administrative codes from the same boundaries as the other layers. - Source: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), [Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org/), volunteer field reports - Part of HOT disaster response exports on HDX by [HOT](https://www.hotosm.org/)
dct_publisher_sm: OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps, volunteer field reports
